0ff9d9c6-029f-459a-90cd-9f88518a3c83.body: Oliveira has 32 finishes in 37 wins and averages 1.2 takedowns, 1.1 submission attempts and 3.7 minutes of control a fight, but he is 47% on takedown defense, and his last five include a knockout loss to Topuria. Lopes is the heavier volume man at 56 significant strikes a fight with 24 finishes in 28 wins, and he knocked out Steve Garcia and Jean Silva before losing twice to Volkanovski. A title fight over five rounds gives Oliveira time to find the choke and Lopes time to stack damage.
0ff9d9c6-029f-459a-90cd-9f88518a3c83.take: Lopes brings 56 strikes a fight and 24 finishes in 28 wins. A knockout over Jean Silva and another over Steve Garcia show the power is real, and five rounds is a lot of time to land it.

edd40b01-005f-4b7f-b115-7f9cc7c502ac.headline: Pavlovich vs Pereira: a 21-3 finisher with an 84-inch reach
edd40b01-005f-4b7f-b115-7f9cc7c502ac.body: Pavlovich has 16 finishes in 21 wins and averages 0.71 knockdowns a fight, but only 24 significant strikes, which means he scores in bursts rather than volume. He knocked out Tallison Teixeira in 39 seconds in May and lost to Aspinall (knockout) and Volkov (decision). Pereira is 13-4 with 11 finishes, lost to Gane last time, and is moving up to heavyweight. The reach is 84 inches for Pavlovich against 79 for Pereira, so Pavlovich gets to throw first.
edd40b01-005f-4b7f-b115-7f9cc7c502ac.take: Pavlovich averages 0.71 knockdowns a fight, which is 5.7 points before he adds a finish bonus. His 24 strikes a fight means the points come as one big hit.

599c4207-f5be-4a69-8e56-1c84ef6eeae5.headline: Moreno vs Johnson: pace and pressure against a man who has been caught
599c4207-f5be-4a69-8e56-1c84ef6eeae5.body: Moreno throws 75 significant strikes a fight and adds 1.1 takedowns and over two minutes of control, and he has beaten Morales, Erceg and Albazi while losing to Taira by knockout. Charles Johnson is 20-9 and has been finished by Almabayev (submission) and Alex Perez (knockout) in his last five. Over three rounds, Moreno's volume wears on him, and at 58% takedown defense Johnson gives Moreno a second way to score.
599c4207-f5be-4a69-8e56-1c84ef6eeae5.take: Moreno wins by accumulation: 75 strikes, 1.1 takedowns, more than two minutes of control. Nothing is spectacular, but all of it counts, and he has been doing it against better opposition.

7e21c0ee-7b11-41ad-a889-3affa12ba80d.headline: Moreno vs Johnson: pace and pressure against a man who has been caught
7e21c0ee-7b11-41ad-a889-3affa12ba80d.body: Moreno throws 75 significant strikes a fight and adds 1.1 takedowns and over two minutes of control, and he has beaten Morales, Erceg and Albazi while losing to Taira by knockout. c0fbd52b-48f3-4029-80ad-1a8acd04077b.headline: Pasley vs Tafa: a 4-0 prospect, a 7-6 knockout artist and one big shot
c0fbd52b-48f3-4029-80ad-1a8acd04077b.body: Quentin Pasley is 24, 4-0 with four finishes, and knocked out Arlind Berisha last time. Junior Tafa is 7-6 with seven finishes of his own, including knockouts of Christian and Sharaf, but Baraniewski knocked him out last time. Tafa stops 84% of takedowns, so Pasley's 1.0 takedowns a fight may not be the way in. Both throw to finish, and Tafa has the kind of shot that ends a prospect's run.
c0fbd52b-48f3-4029-80ad-1a8acd04077b.take: Pasley is 4-0 with four finishes and the length at 76 inches. A win over a veteran is how he becomes a name, so expect him to push the pace.

16ac005e-d09b-45c6-a63d-72d36bb79884.headline: Pasley vs Tafa: a 4-0 prospect, a 7-6 knockout artist and one big shot
16ac005e-d09b-45c6-a63d-72d36bb79884.body: Quentin Pasley is 24, 4-0 with four finishes, and knocked out Arlind Berisha last time. de2e9610-3fa5-48e6-9694-920d18deae5f.headline: Conceicao vs Rojas: a submission hunter meets a man with no takedown defense on paper
de2e9610-3fa5-48e6-9694-920d18deae5f.body: Roque Conceicao is 12-3 with 11 finishes and won by submission over Chavez, but a knockout loss to Rodriguez and a decision loss to Araujo mean he has dropped two straight. Nilson Rojas is 9-1, 27 years old, lands 42 strikes a fight and was knocked out by Bilal Hasan last time. His takedown defense is listed at 0%, which is exactly the opening a man with 0.7 submission attempts a fight is looking for.
de2e9610-3fa5-48e6-9694-920d18deae5f.take: Conceicao needs the mat. With 11 finishes in 12 wins and Rojas at 0% on takedown defense, a choke is the realistic way out of the two-fight skid.

c4f7c95b-1429-4082-8727-28488d54b447.headline: Conceicao vs Rojas: a submission hunter meets a man with no takedown defense on paper
c4f7c95b-1429-4082-8727-28488d54b447.body: Roque Conceicao is 12-3 with 11 finishes and won by submission over Chavez, but a knockout loss to Rodriguez and a decision loss to Araujo mean he has dropped two straight. bc0c8860-fd98-4f47-9d51-68a0d1df47e2.headline: Hill vs Dyer: a 35-fight veteran against a 25-year-old who knocks people out
bc0c8860-fd98-4f47-9d51-68a0d1df47e2.body: Angela Hill has been in 35 pro fights and lands 65 significant strikes a fight, but she has lost three of her last five on the scorecards. Shanelle Dyer is 25, 8-1 with 6 finishes, and knocked out Elise Reed and Ravena Oliveira back to back. Dyer is 3 inches taller at 66 inches and lands 60 strikes a fight herself, so this is a volume fight with one fighter who hits harder.
bc0c8860-fd98-4f47-9d51-68a0d1df47e2.take: Hill has the experience and the volume, 65 strikes and 0.9 takedowns a fight. She wins on pace if it goes the distance, because her 56% takedown defense says she isn't running from a scramble.

3d195496-bd22-48de-b5dd-4f3943c8735e.headline: Hill vs Dyer: a 35-fight veteran against a 25-year-old who knocks people out
3d195496-bd22-48de-b5dd-4f3943c8735e.body: Angela Hill has been in 35 pro fights and lands 65 significant strikes a fight, but she has lost three of her last five on the scorecards. Shanelle Dyer is 25, 8-1 with 6 finishes, and knocked out Elise Reed and Ravena Oliveira back to back. a382b001-2dc4-40be-8247-5ad62b8d63a7.headline: Susurkaev vs Pinas: a 12-0 grappler against the man who hits like a truck
a382b001-2dc4-40be-8247-5ad62b8d63a7.body: Pinas is the most dangerous puncher on this card: he averages 1.5 knockdowns a fight, has knocked out his last four opponents (Pulyaev, Almeida, Schultz, Costa) and has finished all 11 of his wins. If Susurkaev can get inside the 79-inch reach and clinch, he turns the knockout into a wrestling match.
a382b001-2dc4-40be-8247-5ad62b8d63a7.take: Susurkaev has to get close. At 1.3 takedowns and 0.5 knockdowns a fight, he can score on both feet and mat, and his submission win says he finishes from top.

666c961c-228c-4051-a784-bf7aa8166a1b.body: Pinas is the most dangerous puncher on this card: he averages 1.5 knockdowns a fight, has knocked out his last four opponents (Pulyaev, Almeida, Schultz, Costa) and has finished all 11 of his wins. 87895009-0d60-42b6-b269-c7b1ba7da185.headline: Humphrey vs Veretennikov: a 5-0 wrestler with a 77-inch reach meets a 36-year-old who has been knocked out twice lately
87895009-0d60-42b6-b269-c7b1ba7da185.body: Ronald Humphrey is 5-0 with five finishes, averages 2.0 takedowns, 2 minutes of control and 0.5 knockdowns a fight, and submitted Alexis Miranda last time. Nikolay Veretennikov is 14-8 and 36, with a knockout over Niko Price but knockout losses to Khaos Williams and Vanderford in his last five. He lands 17 strikes a fight and stops 59% of takedowns, so Humphrey has room to work.
87895009-0d60-42b6-b269-c7b1ba7da185.take: Humphrey is the prospect with the full toolbox: 2.0 takedowns (4 points), over 2 minutes of control and 0.5 knockdowns a fight. A 5-0 start with five finishes is what finish bonuses are made of.

e8582c5e-bb72-4a71-a3de-cb5555701fac.headline: Humphrey vs Veretennikov: a 5-0 wrestler with a 77-inch reach meets a 36-year-old who has been knocked out twice lately
e8582c5e-bb72-4a71-a3de-cb5555701fac.body: Ronald Humphrey is 5-0 with five finishes, averages 2.0 takedowns, 2 minutes of control and 0.5 knockdowns a fight, and submitted Alexis Miranda last time. e8d4f9af-95ce-4a04-a97b-631812e12892.headline: Hooper vs Padilla: a southpaw grappler against an 89-strike striker
e8d4f9af-95ce-4a04-a97b-631812e12892.body: Chase Hooper averages 12 significant strikes but 2.4 takedowns, 3.3 minutes of control and 0.6 submission attempts a fight, and his takedown defense is only 33%. Hooper has been knocked out twice in his last five (Gibson, Hernandez). If Padilla stays on his feet he outstrikes him by a distance, and if Hooper gets in close it is a different fight.
e8d4f9af-95ce-4a04-a97b-631812e12892.take: Hooper is a pure grappler: 2.4 takedowns, 3.3 minutes of control. But those knockouts in his last five say he gets hurt on the way in.

95475717-175a-4ee1-9fad-c41255432ece.headline: Hooper vs Padilla: a southpaw grappler against an 89-strike striker
95475717-175a-4ee1-9fad-c41255432ece.body: Chase Hooper averages 12 significant strikes but 2.4 takedowns, 3.3 minutes of control and 0.6 submission attempts a fight, and his takedown defense is only 33%. 9360b72a-5495-4045-94c2-2928a56d4a51.headline: Barber vs Judice: a grinder against a 78-strike southpaw with real power
9360b72a-5495-4045-94c2-2928a56d4a51.body: Maycee Barber is 15-3 and averages 1.5 takedowns and 2.8 minutes of control a fight, but her takedown defense is listed at 35% and Alexa Grasso knocked her out last time. Carli Judice is 27, 7-2, a southpaw who lands 78 strikes a fight with 0.5 knockdowns and has won four of her last five, with knockouts over Chaves, Caliari and Duben. Barber has been better against everyone who isn't a clean striker, and this is a clean striker.
9360b72a-5495-4045-94c2-2928a56d4a51.take: Barber wins by getting it down: 1.5 takedowns and nearly 3 minutes of control a fight. But after the Grasso knockout, she has to be careful about the exchanges on the way in.

4c22b34d-e814-4f07-ba25-61ede1891fd1.headline: Barber vs Judice: a grinder against a 78-strike southpaw with real power
4c22b34d-e814-4f07-ba25-61ede1891fd1.body: Maycee Barber is 15-3 and averages 1.5 takedowns and 2.8 minutes of control a fight, but her takedown defense is listed at 35% and Alexa Grasso knocked her out last time. 4a43046a-2e79-41ce-bec3-b3fb34940c2a.headline: Phillips vs Ewing: a 3.5-takedown wrestler on a four-fight skid meets a rising striker
4a43046a-2e79-41ce-bec3-b3fb34940c2a.body: Kyler Phillips has lost three straight, but he is a wrestler through and through: 3.5 takedowns and 3.5 minutes of control a fight with 84% takedown defense. Ethyn Ewing is 10-2, lands 67 strikes a fight, defends 100% of takedowns and knocked out Rafael Estevam last time. Those three losses, to Jourdain, Oliveira and Font, all went to the scorecards, so he is hard to put away but has not been winning the rounds.
4a43046a-2e79-41ce-bec3-b3fb34940c2a.take: Phillips is the grappler: 3.5 takedowns is 7 points a fight and 3.5 minutes of control is 3.5 more. He needs it on the mat to turn the skid around.

f3fc2490-afed-4005-9767-ba08acd0edb6.headline: Phillips vs Ewing: a 3.5-takedown wrestler on a four-fight skid meets a rising striker
f3fc2490-afed-4005-9767-ba08acd0edb6.body: Kyler Phillips has lost three straight, but he is a wrestler through and through: 3.5 takedowns and 3.5 minutes of control a fight with 84% takedown defense. f3fc2490-afed-4005-9767-ba08acd0edb6.take: Ewing has 67 strikes a fight and 100% takedown defense, and recently knocked out Estevam. His style is to stay on his feet and outscore wrestlers.

1b3a1b71-0094-4677-85a8-344d89863365.headline: Cavalcanti vs Montague: a volume striker against a woman who holds you down for 7 minutes
1b3a1b71-0094-4677-85a8-344d89863365.body: Michelle Montague is 8-0, averages 2.3 takedowns and 7.5 minutes of control a fight, and has beaten Mayra Bueno Silva on points. Jacqueline Cavalcanti is 10-2 and lands 72 strikes a fight, with 89% takedown defense, but she lost to Ketlen Vieira last time. If Cavalcanti keeps it standing she can outwork her, but with Montague's control time, a single takedown early can set the tone for the round.
1b3a1b71-0094-4677-85a8-344d89863365.take: Cavalcanti has the volume (72 strikes) and the takedown defense (89%). Her plan is to stay long and win rounds on her feet.

bc0f0236-f28a-4234-9836-39bbe5deb6c8.headline: Cavalcanti vs Montague: a volume striker against a woman who holds you down for 7 minutes
bc0f0236-f28a-4234-9836-39bbe5deb6c8.body: Michelle Montague is 8-0, averages 2.3 takedowns and 7.5 minutes of control a fight, and has beaten Mayra Bueno Silva on points. d60ea446-3ed8-4587-a0ac-e5c6bba78b5d.headline: Kazama vs Garza: a man who has been finished three times meets 82 strikes a fight
d60ea446-3ed8-4587-a0ac-e5c6bba78b5d.body: Toshiomi Kazama is 11-5 and has been knocked out by Elijah Smith, Armfield and Nakamura in his last four, with one submission win over Grigoriou in between. He lands only 7.5 strikes a fight. John Garza is 6-2 and throws 82 a fight, with 77% takedown defense, and lost to Farid Basharat on the scorecards last time. If this stays on the feet, the volume gap is enormous, and Kazama's chin is the question.
d60ea446-3ed8-4587-a0ac-e5c6bba78b5d.take: Kazama has to find the submission or the takedown again, because on the feet he lands a tenth of what Garza does and keeps getting stopped.

38fb3e94-1fff-4912-856b-90d01516cd24.headline: Kazama vs Garza: a man who has been finished three times meets 82 strikes a fight
38fb3e94-1fff-4912-856b-90d01516cd24.body: Toshiomi Kazama is 11-5 and has been knocked out by Elijah Smith, Armfield and Nakamura in his last four, with one submission win over Grigoriou in between. 38fb3e94-1fff-4912-856b-90d01516cd24.take: Garza's 82 strikes a fight is the best volume in this matchup by far. Coming off a decision loss, he wants to make the case that his pace can beat a fighter who has been finished three times.

768eb8d8-9446-44e5-8aba-abb601e2d3a0.headline: Zaynukov vs Guaylupo: two unbeatens, one with a takedown game and one we haven't seen
768eb8d8-9446-44e5-8aba-abb601e2d3a0.body: Magomed Zaynukov is 9-0, trains in the Nurmagomedov school, and averages 74 strikes and 2.0 takedowns a fight with 86% takedown defense, winning on decision over Rzepecki and Caldas. Piero Guaylupo is 12-0 with 10 finishes, a Peruvian who fights out of Los Perros Sarnosos, and he has little UFC data yet. Ten finishes in 12 wins says he ends fights, so the question is whether Zaynukov's wrestling can take away his chance to.
768eb8d8-9446-44e5-8aba-abb601e2d3a0.take: Zaynukov's whole style is takedown, control and decision. 2.0 takedowns and 74 strikes a fight add up, and 86% takedown defense makes it hard to get him down.

0e083532-f501-4493-9f05-577f6c736a85.headline: Zaynukov vs Guaylupo: two unbeatens, one with a takedown game and one we haven't seen
0e083532-f501-4493-9f05-577f6c736a85.body: Magomed Zaynukov is 9-0, trains in the Nurmagomedov school, and averages 74 strikes and 2.0 takedowns a fight with 86% takedown defense, winning on decision over Rzepecki and Caldas. b5fa905d-2d39-41b2-bb71-447aed0499d8.headline: Ferreira vs Mederos: a veteran with 20 wins against 111 strikes a fight
b5fa905d-2d39-41b2-bb71-447aed0499d8.body: MarQuel Mederos lands 111 significant strikes a fight, the highest volume on this part of the card, and is 12-1 with a knockout over Mason Jones last time. Diego Ferreira is 20-7 with 12 finishes, has beaten Quarantillo and knocked out Rebecki and Michael Johnson, but he was knocked out by Alexander Hernandez and lost to Grant Dawson. Ferreira's takedown defense is 51%, and Mederos wants a pace fight where he piles up strikes.
b5fa905d-2d39-41b2-bb71-447aed0499d8.take: Ferreira is the veteran with knockout power and a record of beating gatekeepers. If Mederos stays at distance, he needs one clean shot to flip the volume deficit.

b56a6403-3f05-4a10-8026-7cca89f11b49.headline: Ferreira vs Mederos: a veteran with 20 wins against 111 strikes a fight
b56a6403-3f05-4a10-8026-7cca89f11b49.body: MarQuel Mederos lands 111 significant strikes a fight, the highest volume on this part of the card, and is 12-1 with a knockout over Mason Jones last time. b56a6403-3f05-4a10-8026-7cca89f11b49.take: Mederos at 111 strikes a fight is a points machine. That is over 11 points from strikes alone, and he added 0.5 knockdowns a fight.

f45a78ba-e336-4cf4-b50b-80a5cc2db188.headline: Njokuani vs Bahamondes: four losses in a row against a man who beats strikers
f45a78ba-e336-4cf4-b50b-80a5cc2db188.body: Chidi Njokuani is a Muay Thai striker, 26-12 and 75 inches with an 80-inch reach, but he has lost four straight (Leal, Matthews, Oleksiejczuk, Rodrigues), and the last three were stoppages. Ignacio Bahamondes is 18-7 with 13 finishes, a Chilean striker who won by submission over Jalin Turner and by knockout over Manuel Torres, though he lost to Fiziev and Musayev on points. Njokuani's whole fight is the reach. The risk is he keeps getting caught.
f45a78ba-e336-4cf4-b50b-80a5cc2db188.take: Njokuani needs to use the 80-inch reach and keep this at the end of his strikes. He lands 51 a fight, and a fifth straight loss would be a hard result.

896538f2-8354-42a0-8b03-5ef01522da80.body: Chidi Njokuani is a Muay Thai striker, 26-12 and 75 inches with an 80-inch reach, but he has lost four straight (Leal, Matthews, Oleksiejczuk, Rodrigues), and the last three were stoppages. 896538f2-8354-42a0-8b03-5ef01522da80.take: Bahamondes has 13 finishes in 18 wins and has beaten Turner by submission. He is the more complete finisher in this matchup.

cdc2f6d4-9aa0-42c7-b234-856f1c25bbed.headline: Neal vs Curtis: two men who have lost a lot and still hit hard

Michael Morales is 19-0 with 15 finishes, 79-inch reach, and knocked out Sean Brady, Gilbert Burns and Neil Magny. Both are 100% or near on takedown defense. This is five rounds between two men who hit to finish.
1ac4fbdd-0c83-4373-8632-9195ea05a19a.take: Morales is 19-0 with an 79-inch reach and knockout wins over Brady, Burns and Magny. He is the unbeaten champion-level fighter in the fight.

60cfd80b-0450-4ad1-a979-f15464f99a81.body: Joshua Van is 18-2 and lands 113 significant strikes a fight, over 11 points by volume, and has beaten Pantoja twice, once by knockout. Manel Kape is a southpaw who has knocked out Horiguchi, Royval, Almabayev, da Silva and Osbourne in a row, 20 finishes in 23 wins. It is five rounds, volume against the knockout, and Van's 84% takedown defense and Kape's 90% mean wrestling is not the answer for either.

7de720a9-81c6-4b45-a47a-be3afc71e6bb.take: Jiniushiyue has fought 21 times and is a southpaw. The experience advantage is real if Suzuki hasn't seen the angle.

59743ab9-358b-4d7d-b3fa-35365a8675af.body: Rabindra Dhant is 11-1 with 9 finishes, fighting out of LocknRoll MMA in Nepal, and ends nearly everything he wins. Tajima is the more experienced man and the one more likely to take it to the scorecards.
59743ab9-358b-4d7d-b3fa-35365a8675af.take: Dhant has finished 9 of 11 wins. He is the one in this fight who ends things, and a finish bonus is realistic.

Kaan Ofli is 15-4 and submitted Javier Reyes last time, but Mairon Santos knocked him out and his takedown defense is listed at 0%. That is a bad number against a man averaging nearly three takedowns a fight.
66c459d1-463e-4ce5-add9-4c15d26edc9f.take: Ofli's best result was a submission win. With 0% takedown defense on paper, he has to keep Brito off him or turn the scramble into his own submission.

If Whittaker wrestles, Guskov's 23% is a problem, and if it stays standing, both can end it.
16280daf-6604-4af2-a7be-602464efc64d.take: Guskov has finished almost everyone he has beaten. At 23% takedown defense, though, he has to land first.

61e0e067-1412-47f1-a39f-dbc82d86020a.take: Salkilld's 0.91 knockdowns a fight is 7.3 points a fight on only 10 strikes. He wins fights with one punch.
